scope: External methodology notes explain the domain; they do not replace the supplied CSV or establish which methodology revision produced this export.

indicators.label: Energy supply
indicators.explanation: Estimated energy available from cereals and their products, expressed as a national per-person daily average. This is availability, not measured energy intake.

indicators.label: Dietary fibre supply
indicators.explanation: Estimated dietary fibre available from cereals and their products, expressed as a national per-person daily average. This is availability, not measured fibre intake.

methodSummary: FAO combines national food supply and utilization statistics to estimate food available for people. Nutrient conversion tables connect food quantities to nutrient amounts. Per-person estimates use the population for the corresponding year. These national estimates do not describe how food is distributed among people or the amounts they actually eat. The Global Nutrient Conversion Table (NCT) draws on 13 food composition tables selected from around the world. Their quality was assessed using the FAO/INFOODS Evaluation Framework for food composition tables and databases. This quality screening concerns the composition data; it does not make national availability a measurement of individual intake.
foodGroupSummary: The published food grouping includes rice, maize, wheat, sorghum, millet and other cereals, with derived products. Its boundaries exclude some cereal-based snacks. The classification is a reference for the group; the aggregate CSV cannot reveal the commodities or proportions behind a country’s value.
flagSummary: E — Estimated value is supplied directly in every CSV row. It is not a confidence interval, and the CSV does not identify the estimation procedure for each observation.

collectionSummary: National data are collected through questionnaires, official websites, official trade data, publications, specialized institutions and literature review. This domain-level description was supplied by the user; it does not identify which source was used for each country/year observation.
coverageSummary: The supplied domain metadata describes 178 countries and territories, using FAOSTAT geography and UN M49 codes, with nutrients disaggregated by FAO/WHO GIFT food groups. The active cereals exercise contains only the 43 countries present in the original CSV, for 2019–2023. Domain coverage does not imply that every country has data for every year.
supplementalSummary: The supplemental result contains Calcium supply (4009) for All food groups (FG0), in mg/cap/d: 2,411 observations across 178 countries and territories, 2010–2023. There are 81 absent country–year combinations within that grid, no duplicate observation keys and no blank values. Every row is labelled Estimated value. These observations are kept separate from the cereals energy and fibre exercise. The SQL file is a SELECT query template with food-group and indicator parameters; their bindings are not recorded. It does not document nutrient calculations.
contactSummary: The supplied catalog entries name the FAO Statistics Division (ESS), Crops, Livestock and Food Statistics Team as point of contact and custodian. These are organizational roles. The message “There are no views created for this resource yet” appears to concern a catalog preview; it is not evidence that nutrient methodology is missing. The underlying contact-resource pages were not independently verified.
